tasks.title: Define chat contracts and revocation semantics
criteria: Create contracts/openapi.json, a versioned OpenAPI 3.1 document for agent registration and approval, administrator and moderator sessions, room creation and approval, membership approval and roles, questions and answers, messages, and revocation of a membership and of all chat access.

Create contracts/asyncapi.json, a versioned AsyncAPI document for the realtime stream of messages to connected agents and the console, including the durable cursor and catch-up after a disconnect, using server-sent events with HTTP posts as the intent assumes.

Create docs/domain/model.md describing the identity, rooms, deliberation, messaging, moderation and delivery modules, their state transitions, and how each of the nine invariants in docs/architecture.md is upheld.
Fix the revocation bound in the contracts at the D2 assumption in docs/intent/agent-chat.md: under one second for connected stream clients and the next request for polling clients.
State in the contracts whether a message accepted before a revocation may land after it, as invariant 4 requires, and define the authorization cache epoch that a revocation advances.
Describe the D3 to D7 assumptions of docs/intent/agent-chat.md in the contracts and mark each one as an assumption, not as an owner decision.

Encode the D8 consensus protocol: roles pleb, consul and dispatcher, the 400 ms routing bound, absolute majority floor(k/2)+1, at most three rounds, escalation to an administrator and fallback to all active consuls with a recorded reason.

Add a contract check to make verify, using Node built-ins only, that fails when either document is not valid JSON, declares the wrong specification version or leaves an operation without a response definition.
Change package.json only to add scripts, do not change its dependencies, and add no package.
make verify passes.

tasks.title: Implement question routing through JEV
criteria: Implement ModelPort for one typed call with a dispatcher adapter that uses @typesafe-ai/sdk and zod to call Jev, the System One model of the TypeSafe API, and a fake adapter that can return refusals, timeouts, invalid choices and duplicate deliveries, with no agent framework (D9 and D10).

Run JEV as an agent with the dispatcher role, provisioned by the installation bootstrap (D9 assumption), with a registration, approval, credential, heartbeat and the normal revocation path; the model identity comes from configuration and is not chosen in code.

Send JEV the question and the role roster only, through routing.requested, never the room history, with no tool access, and take the routing decision as a typed choice of the TypeSafe API, not validated after free-form generation.

Accept a routing decision that is exactly one of selected, with exactly one active consul identifier of that room and a short rationale label, or not-for-consul, for a question that is not about software and its implementation, which selects no consul.

Reject an invalid decision, including a selection of JEV itself, of a pleb or of a revoked consul, with 422 and let JEV resubmit within the limit; reject a decision after the 3000 ms limit with 409; never let JEV answer.

Measure the 400 ms target and the 3000 ms limit from sending routing.requested, when the question reaches the head of the queue, to committing the routing decision, including validation and the synchronous audit write; a decision after 400 ms but within 3000 ms stands and the audit records the overrun.
Route questions one at a time in order of acceptance across the installation, and send JEV routing.requested for the next question only after the previous one has a routing decision or is skipped.

Skip a question with skipReason timeout when no valid decision commits within 3000 ms, and at once with skipReason dispatcher-revoked when JEV is revoked while routing; a cold or unavailable JEV is a missing decision, nothing falls back to other consuls, and no confidence rule is added (D9 assumption).

Record routing decisions in a routing_decisions table, audit every routing decision, including rejected attempts and overruns, and every skip with actor and time, and record JEV availability, latency and routing error rate; state in verification.md that fake-adapter tests do not prove real-model latency or routing quality.

HTTP and stream behavior matches contracts/openapi.json and contracts/asyncapi.json; a required contract change is reported as blocked instead of being made here.

tasks.title: Implement the deliberation and the consul answer
criteria: Open a deliberation with its own identity for each pleb question in state routing, and move it to answering when JEV selects a consul, to declined on a not-for-consul decision, to skipped with a skipReason, and to answered when the selected consul answers.

On a not-for-consul decision, post in the room a message of kind dispatcher-reply, authored by JEV, whose body is exactly "This is not a question for a consul."; this fixed reply is the only message JEV ever posts.

Send deliberation.consul-selected with the deliberation id and the question to the selected consul only, and send deliberation.skipped with the deliberation id and the skipReason to the asking pleb and the console.

Implement submitAnswer (POST /v1/deliberations/{deliberationId}/answer) so that only the selected consul answers, once, and the answer is published as answer.published; reject any other caller with 403.
Set no answer deadline: a deliberation stays answering until the selected consul answers or is revoked (D11).
Let no pleb, no person and not JEV publish an answer, and show plebs the final answer, the fixed reply or that the question was skipped.

Keep the deliberation as an explicit transition table over PostgreSQL with no votes table and no in-memory statechart, and implement no proposals, rounds, majority, quorum, escalation or fallback to all active consuls (D8 and D10).

Provide an application operation that skips an answering deliberation with skipReason consul-revoked when its selected consul is revoked before it answers (D11 assumption), covered by tests; the revocation change invokes it.
Audit every answer and every skip with actor and time so an administrator can inspect the provenance.

tasks.title: Implement instant revocation
criteria: Implement the moderation module: an administrator or moderator revokes one room membership or all chat access, the latter as one action, each with an audit record of actor, reason and time.
Advance a revocation epoch that the service edge checks on every request, and cache an authorization decision only with an explicit epoch (invariants 2 and 5).
Reject with 403 a request whose authorization check begins after the revocation commits (D2).

Re-check the subject's authorization epoch before writing each stream event, so no event is written to the revoked subject after the revocation commits; a room revocation stops that room's stream, an all-chat revocation closes the connection, and the revocation propagates to every instance (D2).
Make a revocation reversible only by a new approval, keeping history and auditing every transition (invariant 6 and D5).

Invoke the deliberation skip operation when the selected consul of an answering deliberation is revoked, so the question is skipped with skipReason consul-revoked (D11 assumption), and skip the question being routed at once with skipReason dispatcher-revoked when JEV is revoked.
Test a revocation racing an in-flight message and prove that a message whose insert committed before the revocation keeps its sequence and stays in history.
